content:
The first paragraph identifies Japan and India as sources of silver for China in the late 1500s.  
By this period, after the Spanish established Manila in 1571, the Manila Galleons brought huge quantities of silver from the Americas (New World) to China in exchange for Chinese goods. This trans-Pacific silver flow soon exceeded silver from Japan and Europe combined.  

Central Asia (A) was historically part of the Silk Road trade, but by 1600 it was not the greatest additional source of silver.  
Europe (B) did supply some silver, but not as much as the New World via the Spanish Philippines.  
The Middle East (C) was not a major silver source to China in this period.  

Thus, the greatest volume of additional silver came from the New World.  

Final answer: (D)
